summary: In this excerpt from Book 10, the narrator recounts a day spent in bed and on the sofa after a traumatic experience, vomiting and ignoring messages and visitors. Rhindquist, the CEO of the Company, arrives battered and sad, hugs the narrator, and spends the night with him watching comedy films such as Blazing Saddles and The Princess Bride. The next morning Rhindquist admits he chose the narrator for the job because he thought he was naive, and the narrator, feeling no better, watches another film, Horsefeathers, with him.
one_line: The narrator recovers from a distressing ordeal at home as CEO Rhindquist spends a night watching comedies with him and explains why he chose him.
key_facts: The narrator spent the previous night throwing up and was unsure whether he would go to the office.
The narrator did not go to work the previous day and stayed on the sofa in his shorts watching movies.
The narrator put his loud, angry watch under his pillow and ignored messages appearing on his TV.
The narrator did not answer a knock on his door after lunch because he was watching Wall Street.
Rhindquist pounded on the door, and the narrator woke after 18h and opened it.
Rhindquist looked sad and beaten and gave the narrator a hug before sitting on the sofa.
Rhindquist put on the comedy Blazing Saddles, followed by The Princess Bride, and they watched movies all night.
When the narrator woke in bed, Rhindquist had covered him with a blanket and was asleep on the sofa.
Rhindquist's phone was on the TV with its batteries on the floor.
The narrator ate three bowls of cereal, some toast and an apple for breakfast.
Rhindquist drank a GatorCola from the narrator's fridge and burped in the kitchen.
Rhindquist said, "You've been in my shoes now. Wouldn't you do anything to get out of them?"
Rhindquist said he thought the narrator was "ignorant enough to enjoy it" and later "naive enough to just do the job, take the perks, and sleep well at night."
Rhindquist said, "I was wrong. You're too smart."
The narrator went back to the sofa and put on Horsefeathers, which Rhindquist watched with him.
